Less than four months ago, Bank of America’s chief executive, Brian T. Moynihan, volunteered in a TV interview what he would say to his 210,000 employees about the chance of artificial intelligence replacing human work.

“You don’t have to worry,” he said. “It’s not a threat to their jobs.”

Last week, after Bank of America reported $8.6 billion in profit for the first quarter — $1.6 billion more than the same period a year earlier — Mr. Moynihan struck a different tone.

The bank’s bottom line, he said, was helped by shedding 1,000 jobs through attrition by “eliminating work and applying technology,” which he repeatedly specified was artificial intelligence. He predicted more of that in the months and years to come.

column15: Useful augmentation/workforce culture row because it rewards employees for using AI in their own work or improving team performance. However, credible commitment is medium because the source is a communications trade article quoting an internal memo.

column4: “We want to make people’s jobs easier so they can focus on higher-value tasks and enabling best-in-class products and experiences for our customers.”
column5: Productivity in the Age of Intelligent Automation
column15: Strong augmentation row. Named Comcast AI strategy leader describes AI as helping employees focus on higher-value work, with no stated layoffs or reduced hiring logic.

column4: Comcast is “redefining digital care through an agentic AI transformation” and moving “from scripted bots to modular, autonomous systems of intelligent agents.”
column5: Customer Care Reimagined: Comcast’s Ongoing Agentic AI Journey
column15: This is the strongest automation row. It does not mention layoffs, but it does show AI taking over customer-care workflow steps through autonomous agents.

column4: AI is “automating simpler customer service tasks through chatbots, allowing human agents to focus on complex interactions.”
column5: How AI is Reshaping Unified Communications
column15: I would code this as augmentation because automation is framed as supporting human agents, not reducing headcount. It is useful but less strong because the page does not give a clear publication date.

column4: Comcast says AI-powered network amplifiers can “self-monitor,” “self-heal,” and “self-maintain,” and that AI can “automatically boost capacity to areas where it is needed most.”
column5: Comcast Pushes AI to the Edge to Power the Nation’s Smartest Broadband Network
column15: Task automation row, but not workforce-displacement evidence. It shows AI taking over network monitoring and maintenance tasks through self-monitoring, self-healing, and automatic capacity adjustment, but does not state layoffs or reduced hiring.
